title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-25
content:
2026-03-25 - daily scratchpad (Jordan)

Morning summary:
- Quick triage: high error rate spikes on 2AM-3AM UTC window for model-route `gptx-13b-enc` on dedicated pool alpha. Error signatures point to CUDA OOM + occasional RMM allocator failures.
- Observed 10-15% request lat p90 increase on long-context (>4k) requests after last kernel bump. Need to check fused attention rollback.

Top priorities for the day:
1) Stabilize OOMs for dedicated-pool-alpha (urgent)
   - Reproduce locally with load generator using same seq_len distribution and batch policy (use bench-tool with --seq-dist file).
   - Check PR 789 (Luca) which changed KV cache eviction heuristics; possible memory leak when reusing contexts across requests.
   - Short-term mitigation: tighten per-request memory guardrails and force early KV eviction for route gptx-13b-enc in Dedicated config.
   - Owner: Jordan + Aisha. Expected: deploy hotfix to alpha by EOD if repro confirmed.

2) Perf regression investigation (p90 up for >4k)
   - Hypothesis: fused attention kernel fallback triggered for some ops, adding extra mem copies.
   - Steps: enable kernel tracing (env SERVING_KERNEL_TRACE=1) on a small canary, run 200 long-context requests, collect kernel selection logs.
   - Cross-check with perf counters (nvprof/rocprof) on sample GPU.
   - Linked PR to verify: PR 792 (Mei) changed attention tiling; rollback to previous tile config to confirm.

3) Bug triage notes:
   - JIRA-SERV-1243: intermittent RMM double-free during batch-flatten path. Repro steps in ticket (attached logs). Suspect race in pooled-allocator destructor. Add extra shuffle to stress test.
   - JIRA-SERV-1250: streaming websocket connections sometimes hang after a kernel fallback; root cause might be incomplete token-flush on fallback path. Need to add unit test for partial flush.

Quick commands/recipes to repro: (for self)
- Run local repro for OOM: ./bench/run_loadgen --route gptx-13b-enc --pool dedicated-alpha --duration 600 --seq-dist ./tools/seq_dist/long_tail.json --concurrency 24
- Enable kernel logging: export SERVING_KERNEL_TRACE=1; ./bin/serve --config configs/dedicated-alpha.yaml 2>&1 | tee /tmp/kernel-trace.log
- Heap snapshot script: python tools/heap_snapshot.py --pid <pid> --out /tmp/heap-2026-03-25.json

Notes from yesterday's debugging (carry over):
- Memory growth correlates with requests that use function-calling + structured output; we may be holding onto interim KV for longer due to lack of explicit finish() calls in the function-calling path. Aisha to add patch that ensures clear_kv_on_finish on function-call handler.
- Luca's allocator changes improved small-batch p99 earlier, but might have introduced edge-case for large-history reuse. More unit tests needed for mixed-seq-length batches.

Ideas / experiments to run this week:
- Add a nightly stress job that ramps long-context traffic for 30m against a canary dedicated pool to catch regressions early. (CI job, notify #serving-runtime-debug)
- Try alternative RMM pool settings: RMM_POOL_SIZE_PERCENT=70 (current 85) to see if headroom reduces OOMs under spikes.
- Explore enabling partial KV compression for long-history contexts (>8k tokens) to reduce memory footprint; perf trade-offs TBD.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the recent kernel-selection change (tile-size heuristic) behind the p90 perf regression? Mei to run bisect today.
- Should we add a circuit-breaker to revert to older attention implementation automatically if p90 increases >10% post-deploy? Pro: fast rollback. Con: complexity in routing.
- Need decision on allowing ephemeral extra memory headroom per-tenant vs strict per-request caps for dedicated customers. (Product ask from support: allow short bursts)

Small todos (today):
- [ ] Re-run repro for JIRA-SERV-1243 with shuffle stress (Jordan)
- [ ] Add kernel-trace collection to canary pipeline (Mei)
- [ ] Draft hotfix for memory guardrails config (Aisha)
- [ ] Add unit test for partial token flush on fallback path (Luca)
- [ ] Sync with SRE on autoscaler behavior during spike window (15:00 PT)

Meeting notes / syncs
- 10:30 sync with SRE (Justin) to align on rollback plan and canary gating thresholds.
- 15:00 product sync to discuss burst memory policy for dedicated customers (invite: product-dedicated).

Random scratch thoughts:
- Maybe add a per-route "safety-mode" flag we can toggle from Console to enforce strict memory caps + older kernels for fragile routes. Quick UI flag could be useful for on-call.
- Consider a small telemetry event (route, seq_len, kernel_variant) emitted for 1% of requests to build a map of kernel_variant -> latency distribution over time. Could be surfaced in Console Optimize.

End-of-day goals:
- Confirm repro for OOM and either land hotfix or have rollback plan ready.
- Collect kernel-trace logs and start bisect for perf regression.
- Create follow-up tickets for any longer-term changes (KV compression spike, nightly stress job).

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep canary stable; avoid rolling major kernel changes until we have stress job in place.
- When reproducing, try to replicate request ordering from prod logs (use timestamps) to catch ordering-dependent race.
